title: Canonical tensor coordinates between diagonal and ordered affine purity
statement:
Use the positive finite coefficient setting Q and the canonical shifted-line and degree-zero unit comparisons [def-pur-affine-diagonal-tate-coordinates]. For a k-scheme T, let D_d be Q.diagonalTwist T d, the exact comparison realization of the ordered tensor of d shifted ordinary finite Tate lines [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Let L be shiftedLine Q T and let F_T be tensoring on the right by L, with its ordered action F_T^d as in [def-pur-affine-space-comparison]. Use the published derived tensor and exact-comparison tensor constraint of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]. For every ambient pro-etale derived object M and every d>=0, define the canonical isomorphism
c_(M,d) : M tensor D_d -> F_T^d(M)
as follows. In rank zero it is M tensor the specified diagonal-unit comparison, followed by the right unitor. The coefficient successor is exact comparison monoidality followed by identity on D_d tensor the canonical shifted-line comparison of [def-pur-affine-diagonal-tate-coordinates]. For d+1, tensor this successor constraint with M, apply the inverse associator from M tensor (D_d tensor L) to (M tensor D_d) tensor L, and then apply c_(M,d) tensor identity_L. The actual generic recursion is specialized to the existing coefficient category, and its recorded cached endpoint aliases are identified by the unique isomorphism heterogeneously equal to that recursion. No purity map, arbitrary orientation, finite-Tor hypothesis, or presentation witness enters these coordinates.
